display.purpose: h1; 48 px Bricolage 800 at full width. The hero headline overrides to 44 px (56 px from 600 px) so two lines fit the band.

score.purpose: The lap score alone, 96 px at 90% width, the doubled top step of the ramp.

headline.purpose: h2 screen titles and the 32 px sun-text numbers in stats strips, readouts and the level card.

title.purpose: h3 section heads ruled above in 2 px ink, the masthead wordmark, part points, history scores. Buttons use a 700 / 95%-width / 19 px cut.

body.purpose: Atkinson Hyperlegible 400 at 16 px / 1.45 for sentences and controls; 17 px lead, 15 px inside cards, notices, lists and tables.

label.purpose: 13 px Atkinson 700 uppercase at 0.08em for field labels, stat captions, table headers; chips at 0.04em; tab labels and the level stamp use Bricolage at 13 px.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing; exponential ease-out for the meter grow and the screen rise.

motion.name: meter-grow
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the orange reading growing into the aqua band on the results screen.

motion.name: screen-rise
motion.value: rise .16s var(--ease); @keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(6px) } }
motion.purpose: Screen changes fade and rise 6 px.

motion.name: progress-bar
motion.purpose: The analysis progress bar (#bar) tracks frames linearly; functional, not authored.

motion.name: hero-overlay
motion.purpose: The hero's skeleton canvas fades in once the model has read the frame.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .screen.active, .meter i { animation: none !important; transition: none !important } }
motion.purpose: Removes the grow and the rise.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Gutters open to 24 px, the hero gains a 2 px ink frame and a 16:10 ratio, the form splits 1fr / 1.3fr, the consent sheet centres with a 3 px ink border.

breakpoints.name: column-max
breakpoints.purpose: Maximum width of the main column, the masthead content and the tab bar.

canvasInks.note: draw.js reads --paper-bright, --aqua, --aqua-pale, --aqua-text, --sun, --over, --ink, --ink-2, --hair, --paper-deep via getPropertyValue; the video overlay and report.js carry the same hex values as literals.
canvasInks.composite: globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply' for every orange reading drawn over an aqua target band (angle chart, history chart, report-card band and part bars).

provenance.rasters: app/assets/examples/*.jpg are the owner's own photographs (six real frames, model-verified); the hero uses backstroke_lap.jpg greyscale-multiplied over aqua. The pose model is YOLO11n-pose (ONNX). No generated rasters exist in this build.

narrative.overview:
SafeDive Coach is printed, not rendered. The whole app is one two-ink risograph flyer from a town pool's recreation department: cream paper, an aqua ink, a sun-orange ink, and black for the words. It refuses the category default of white cards, one blue, soft shadows and a hero-metric block. Everything sits flat on the paper and is separated by ruled ink lines, the way a photocopied program is laid out with a ruler, and the density is high because the parent reads it once, on a sunlit deck, with wet hands.

The signature move is that the overprint is the measurement. Aqua and orange are never decoration: aqua prints the target zone, orange prints the swimmer's reading, and wherever the two inks overlap the paper turns deep overprint green. That green is the only "good" colour in the app, and it is never painted directly on a surface; it appears only where a reading has reached its target (the meters, the charts, the hero band). State is overprint, never a fourth colour.

The build keeps the world honest with standard controls. Inputs, buttons, a select, a range, a checkbox and a bottom tab bar are all ordinary web elements given 2 px ink borders and the two inks; the world shows in type, palette, density and the one overprint move, not in invented widgets. Light only: a sunlit deck has no dark mode (`color-scheme: light` is declared and nothing else is themed).
keyCharacteristics: Three inks on paper: aqua, sun-orange, black; green exists only as their overprint.
Overprint as measurement: `mix-blend-mode: multiply` in CSS and `globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'` on every canvas.
Ruled, not carded: 2 px and 3 px ink rules divide content; fills are flat; there are no shadows anywhere.
One display face carries every heading and every number (Bricolage Grotesque 800); one body face carries every sentence (Atkinson Hyperlegible).
A fixed five-step type ramp (13, 16, 22, 32, 48 px) with the score alone at the doubled top step (96 px).
Corners of 3 px on controls and cards, square on meters and rules, a full circle only on the level stamp.
One authored motion: the orange reading growing into the aqua band.

rules.name: The Overprint Rule
rules.body: Green is never a fill you choose. It is what aqua over orange prints, so it may appear on a surface only where a reading has reached its target; write "good" with `--over` for type and borders, and produce it with multiply everywhere a measurement is drawn.

rules.name: The Three-Ink Rule
rules.body: State is overprint, never a fourth colour. Good is green, warning is orange text, bad is ink. No red, no yellow, no grey.

rules.name: The Ink-Tint Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is a tint of ink on paper (`ink-2`), never a grey. Dividers that are not rules are 22% ink (`hair`).

rules.name: The Every-Number Rule
rules.body: Every number that is read as a result (score, points, stats, readouts, history) is set in Bricolage Grotesque 800. Body copy never carries a headline number.

rules.name: The Five-Step Rule
rules.body: Text sizes come from the five-step ramp (13, 16, 22, 32, 48 px) and the score at 96 px. The 15, 17 and 19 px cuts for dense copy, lead copy and button labels are the only in-between sizes the build uses; do not add more.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts. A surface is distinguished from the page by a 2 px ink rule and a paper-bright fill, never by a shadow, a blur or a gradient.

rules.name: The Rule-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy of separation is 3 px ink (chrome and strip tops), 2 px ink (`--rule`, every control, card and section head), 1 px at 22% ink (row dividers). Nothing else.

dos: Do draw every measurement as aqua target plus orange reading with multiply, in CSS (`mix-blend-mode: multiply`) or on canvas (`globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'`), so good prints as overprint green.
Do set every result number in Bricolage Grotesque 800 and every sentence in Atkinson Hyperlegible, from the five-step ramp (13, 16, 22, 32, 48 px); the score alone at 96 px.
Do separate content with ink rules (3 px chrome, 2 px controls and sections, 1 px hairline rows) and flat paper-bright fills on a 3 px trim.
Do use standard web controls (input, select, range, checkbox, button) styled with 2 px ink borders; one solid orange primary per screen, outlined aqua ghosts for everything secondary.
Do keep targets at least 46 px tall (buttons 56, inputs 50, chips 8 x 12 padding, range thumb 28) and keep focus visible as a 3 px aqua outline, for wet one-handed use.
Do read colours from the `:root` custom properties in any new canvas (`getPropertyValue`) so the stylesheet stays the single source of ink.
Do ship only the owner's photographs and the model's own overlays as rasters; keep the greyscale-multiply treatment when a photo must sit in the world.
donts: Don't paint overprint green as a decorative fill; it is produced by overlap, and typed with `--over` only to say "good".
Don't add a fourth colour for state (no red error, no yellow warning, no grey disabled); warn is sun-text, bad is ink, quiet is hairline.
Don't use shadows, gradients, blurs, or a dark theme; the deck has no dark mode and the print has no depth.
Don't use grey for secondary text; use the ink tint (`ink-2`) on paper.
Don't add motion beyond the 600 ms meter grow and the 160 ms screen fade-rise; nothing else moves, and reduced motion removes both.
Don't introduce icon fonts, glyph icons or a component library; icons are inline SVG at 2.2 stroke in `currentColor`, and there are four of them.
Don't round beyond 3 px on anything but the level stamp; meters, bars and rules stay square.
